key_insight: A scaffold-aware foundation model pretrained on small‑molecule natural products produces rich, transferable representations that improve taxonomy classification, genome mining and virtual screening performance.
problem_solved: Existing molecular models struggle to capture scaffold-specific features and taxonomy information for natural products, limiting downstream discovery tasks where labeled data are scarce and structural diversity is high.
method: Pretrain a scaffold-aware encoder on natural product molecules using masked reconstruction objectives to learn local and global chemical context.
Use contrastive learning to align molecular embeddings with scaffold and taxonomy signals, sharpening class separation and transferability.
Fine-tune or apply the pretrained foundation model to downstream tasks (taxonomy classification, genome mining, virtual screening) for improved performance with limited labels.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a reusable pretrained model and representation strategy tailored to natural products, enabling more accurate and data‑efficient drug discovery workflows and cross-task transfer learning.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing pretraining (masked + contrastive) → scaffold-aware embeddings → downstream tasks (taxonomy, genome mining, virtual screening).
Embedding space visualization (2D t-SNE/UMAP) with clusters colored by taxonomic class or scaffold to show improved separation.
Bar/line chart comparing task performance (accuracy/AUROC/enrichment) of the foundation model versus baseline models on taxonomy, genome mining and virtual screening.
Schematic of a molecule annotated with scaffold regions to illustrate the scaffold-aware modeling concept.
paper_title: Pretraining a foundation model for small-molecule natural products
paper_authors: Yuheng Ding, Bo Qiang, Shaoning Li, Yiran Zhou, Jie Yu
